source: ST-LOCK — Agent Naming, SCS Governance Corrections, and Interim Decision Capture (2026-07-24)
note: Real governed Product Owner rulings. The Phase 2 Decision Register must ingest these unchanged. Mirrors app/src/seed/decisions.ts.

decisions.title: ShockBoard supersession
decisions.rationale: Recorded as an existing Product Owner ruling. Superseding artifact and full rationale pending Product Owner confirmation.
decisions.supersededAssumptions: Any prior reliance on ShockBoard as an active surface.
decisions.implementationConsequences: References to ShockBoard are treated as superseded pending confirmation of the replacement.

decisions.title: SCS naming and scope
decisions.ruling: SCS is the ShockTheory Constitutional System product — the governed index, awareness, and artifact-navigation system for ShockTheory OS. It displays authority; it does not manufacture it.
decisions.rationale: Establishes the product identity and boundary so SCS is not confused with an agent or a competing source of truth.
decisions.supersededAssumptions: Treating SCS as a dashboard or as an authority-bearing system.
decisions.implementationConsequences: All copy distinguishes the SCS product from the #SCS build agent.

decisions.title: ProductOS under constitutional review
decisions.ruling: ProductOS is placed under constitutional review.
decisions.rationale: Recorded as an existing Product Owner ruling. Scope and outcome of the review pending Product Owner confirmation.
decisions.supersededAssumptions: Treating ProductOS as settled or authoritative during review.
decisions.implementationConsequences: ProductOS carries a Constitutional Review governance state until the review concludes.

decisions.title: SCS Home versus Executive Snapshot
decisions.ruling: SCS Home is the interactive constitutional command center. Executive Snapshot is the concise, generated operational briefing produced from SCS state.
decisions.rationale: Resolves an architectural conflation before further screens are built.
decisions.supersededAssumptions: The single-screen Executive Snapshot performing the role of Home.
decisions.implementationConsequences: Home and the briefing are separate routes; the briefing stays concise.

decisions.title: Coupled SAPDOS–Kidlytics workstreams
decisions.ruling: SAPDOS and Kidlytics workstreams are coupled.
decisions.rationale: Recorded as an existing Product Owner ruling. Coupling mechanics pending Product Owner confirmation.
decisions.supersededAssumptions: Treating SAPDOS methodology and Kidlytics product work as independent.
decisions.implementationConsequences: Methodology maturity of SAPDOS artifacts is validated through Kidlytics first.

decisions.title: Methodology Maturity
decisions.ruling: Methodology Maturity is an independent field for reusable SAPDOS artifacts: Draft, Validated in Kidlytics, Validated in Additional Products, Reusable Standard, Constitutional Standard. It is never merged with authority, governance status, work state, product maturity, or publication gate.
decisions.rationale: Keeps methodology reusability distinct from other record dimensions.
decisions.supersededAssumptions: Conflating methodology maturity with product or publication maturity.
decisions.implementationConsequences: A distinct Methodology Maturity dimension is added to the data model and UI.

decisions.title: #SOS and #SCS authority boundaries
decisions.ruling: No agent may approve its own proposals. #SOS protects and advises Product Owner authority but does not exercise it. #SCS designs and builds SCS but is not SCS and holds no constitutional authority.
decisions.rationale: Prevents any agent from manufacturing constitutional authority.
decisions.supersededAssumptions: Any implication that an AI agent can approve constitutional decisions.
decisions.implementationConsequences: Authority scope is shown per agent; AI recommends, never approves.

decisions.title: #CKL and #CIA naming and authority boundaries
decisions.ruling: #CKL (ChatGPT Kidlytics) provides Product Owner advisory support, product architecture, specification drafting, product challenge, review, and cross-artifact reconciliation for Kidlytics but does not replace Product Owner approval. #CIA (Claude Kidlytics Invitation AI Agent) evaluates and synthesizes the Kidlytics invitation experience but may not change architecture, canonical language, or product decisions.
decisions.rationale: Names the Kidlytics advisory and invitation agents and bounds their authority.
decisions.supersededAssumptions: Undefined naming for the Kidlytics advisory and invitation agents.
decisions.implementationConsequences: The agent register lists #CKL and #CIA with explicit authority boundaries.
